Pages thin for the Mapuche before 1861 (Arauco War and the Spanish Parlamento de Tapihue pages gave nothing usable): the mapuche dossier's 1810 start is the project's scope, not a founding (confidence 1), and its Argentine half (Puelmapu) uses modern provinces as a reading.

Counterpart strings that are names, not slugs, because the dependency has no dossier: 'Cayman Islands', 'Turks and Caicos Islands', 'Bay Islands' (colony-of-jamaica) and 'Falkland Islands Dependencies' (falkland-islands).

republic-of-cuba-in-arms-ten-years-war (1868-1878) and cuban-nationalists (1895-1899, am-08-h) use the same Wikipedia page 'Republic of Cuba in Arms': the colour agent may want one family and one colour; both use kingdom-of-spain as the Spanish counterpart while captaincy-general-of-cuba is the colony itself.

Type choices for the orchestrator: chan-santa-cruz is type state (Britain recognised it de facto 1850s-1893), west-indies-federation is state (not umbrella), cabanagem-rebels, confederation-of-the-equator, juliana-republic and republic-of-cuba-in-arms-ten-years-war are rebel; british-guiana, british-honduras, colony-of-jamaica, falkland-islands, captaincy-general-of-cuba are colony.

Cross-dossier counterpart fixes suggested in the notes file (argentine-confederation gains name 'nobody'; captaincy-general-of-venezuela 1817 loss names the Cliopatria republic-of-venezuela row of 1811-1814; gran-colombia predecessors); this batch did not edit other agents' files.

Page budget: every dossier used 1-6 pages; mapuche opened six (two thin), british-guiana three, the others one to three. Several single-page dossiers (free-province-of-guayaquil, cabanagem-rebels, confederation-of-the-equator, juliana-republic, republic-of-spanish-haiti, west-indies-federation, colony-of-jamaica) have no second page to cross-check regions.
